expectations.text: Output contains a mechanical identity / decomposition section identifying the three-pool balancing and transfer cost as core mechanics
expectations.evidence: Has full '## Mechanical Identity' with 6 sections. Transfer cost explicitly identified: 'Transfers convert one resource into another at a loss (the transfer cost is a friction/tax mechanic).' Mechanical identity statement: 'You are a manager maintaining three interdependent systems against inevitable entropy, trading inefficiency for stability...'

expectations.text: At least 5 distinct setting concepts are presented
expectations.evidence: 7 settings: Tidal Station (★★★★★), The Apothecary's Equilibrium (★★★★★), Watershed (★★★★), Neural Cascade (★★★★), The Candle Archive (★★★★★), Estuary Protocol (★★★★), The Three Cisterns of Ur-Kesh (★★★★★).

expectations.text: Each setting's three pools correspond to three specific named things in the fiction that make intuitive sense
expectations.evidence: All 7 settings: Tidal Station (tidal turbine fuel / battery storage / grid pressure), Apothecary (Fire Essence / Verdant Extract / Void Compound), Watershed (upstream reservoir / town cistern / irrigation channel), Neural Cascade (dopamine / serotonin / norepinephrine), Candle Archive (East Wing / West Wing / Vault), Estuary Protocol (biodiversity / water quality / vegetation), Ur-Kesh (Temple Cistern / Market Cistern / Field Channels).

expectations.text: At least 2 settings include specific diegetic or semi-diegetic UI concepts for the three pools
expectations.evidence: Multiple highly specific UI hooks: Tidal Station ('analog needle meters mounted on a control panel, not health bars... The HUD IS the control room'); Candle Archive ('three pools are visualized as candelabra — the flame count visible on each'); Apothecary ('literal alchemical vats — cylindrical glass containers with colored liquid at varying fill levels'); Ur-Kesh ('cisterns are drawn as architectural cross-sections — you can see the waterline dropping').

expectations.text: No setting demands high-fidelity 3D animation, complex physics, or real-time action systems
expectations.evidence: All settings are flat UI, 2D, or map-based. Specific art directions: 'flat/minimal art' noted, 'hand-drawn or AI-assisted 2D art', 'map view', 'top-down or flat UI view'. No setting implies 3D or real-time action.

expectations.text: At least 3 settings' Mechanical Mappings explain why transferring between the three things costs something in the fiction
expectations.evidence: All 7 settings: Tidal Station ('loses energy to heat and resistance... you lose 15% in transmission'), Apothecary ('transmutation process wastes a portion'), Watershed ('loses water to pipe leakage and evaporation'), Neural Cascade ('drawing from shared biochemical pathways, reducing another'), Candle Archive ('candles tip, drip, extinguish during movement'), Ur-Kesh ('labor-intensive and loses water to spill and evaporation').

expectations.text: At least one setting frames the accelerating drain as something that makes thematic sense, not just a difficulty curve
expectations.evidence: Multiple settings give narrative reasons: Tidal Station ('storm season worsening — each era of difficulty is a new week of deteriorating weather'), Watershed ('drought deepening — The dry season is a natural, visible escalation'), Neural Cascade ('patient's condition worsens over time — the underlying pathology increases demand'), Candle Archive ('outside world deteriorating — driving more people into the archive'), Ur-Kesh ('seasonal calendar — the player can see the months passing, the solstice approaching').

notes: Perfect score. The Candle Archive and Ur-Kesh settings are especially impressive — the former achieves near-perfect mechanic-fiction fusion, the latter is historically unique in the genre. The UI hooks section showed strong understanding of diegetic interface design.
